title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: Data Center Health Worries Animate Midterm Campaigns
summary: Opposition to the rapid emergence of data centers in states such as Ohio and Arizona has ginned up activism and unified voters. A range of public health issues have played into the resistance.

title: She Needed an EpiPen. But First, an Urgent Care Asked Her To Pay.
summary: An uninsured woman sought help at a Virginia urgent care center after being stung by a wasp. She said she was stunned when the center asked her to pay before giving her a shot to reverse her allergic reaction.

title: The Campaign To Defend Trans Healthcare in Missouri Is Slow Going, on Purpose
summary: The campaign to defend access to transgender healthcare for young people in Missouri is taking an unhurried approach to talking with voters about how the ban on midterm ballots would play out.

title: In California and Other States, Dads Are Now Even With Moms in Paid Leave Claims
summary: The U.S. has no law guaranteeing paid parental leave. But in states with their own programs, more dads are using the benefit, surpassing moms in some states. The growth in popularity comes as Americans increasingly say raising children is unaffordable.

title: Hospital Beds for the Nation’s Sickest Kids Are Disappearing
summary: Hospitals nationwide are cutting intensive services for kids in critical care. Many cite too few patients, staffing shortages, and money problems. As a result, kids who need lifesaving care must travel farther. Pediatricians expect more cutbacks in the wake of federal Medicaid cuts.

title: Jacksonville, Florida’s Gun Violence Is Rooted in Redlining and Homes Built on Toxic Waste
summary: Poisons from Jacksonville, Florida’s “Brown’s Dump” seeped into the lifeblood of residents. The harm to their physical and mental health is tied today to another public health crisis: high rates of gun violence among children.

title: Remember This Acronym Next Time You’re Facing a Big Medical Decision: B.R.A.I.N.
summary: If your doctor recommends a big test or procedure, this tool can help you talk through options collaboratively. It works at a routine checkup or in high-stakes medical situations like childbirth.

title: Many Medicare Patients Could Lose Access to Remote Monitoring Devices
summary: A proposed federal rule could dramatically reduce access to remote patient monitoring programs for people on Medicare. The services aim to keep patients out of the hospital by giving them devices to monitor their health at home, but critics say there isn’t enough oversight.

title: The Cost of Healthcare Is Hitting America Where It Hurts: The Wallet
summary: Rising healthcare costs are upending the lives of Americans. People are forgoing health insurance, rationing medications, cutting back on doctor visits, and putting off health procedures they can’t afford. But bringing the costs down won’t be easy.
